requirements_summary: Mid-market SaaS product team evaluating Redwood Hosted API first, then Dedicated reserved capacity if economics justify. Primary workload: embeddings + semantic search for in-app product docs and support KB. Expected steady-state: 60k–120k embedding vectors generated per month (mix of nightly batch jobs and realtime onboarding), 8k–20k semantic search queries/day with 200–400 concurrent low-latency requests during peak. Targets: average search latency <200ms end-to-end, embedding batch throughput 10k vectors/hour during nightly runs. Needs vector DB integration (Pinecone existing; exploring FAISS on-prem for cold-storage), nightly batch pipelines, incremental reindexing, and reranking flow that uses a smaller cross-encoder for top-K refinement. Cost sensitive: wants estimates showing Dedicated reserved capacity breaks even within 6–9 months versus Hosted. Security: SOC2 + SSO/SAML, audit logs, KMS for key management, optional EU data residency for EU customers. Must support rollout plan (canary + auto-fallback to cheaper model variant).
notes: Customer quote: 'We need search to feel instant inside the app — users won't tolerate slow results.'
POC plan: run 2-week Hosted API POC using anonymized subset of KB (~5k docs) then pilot on Dedicated if Hosted cost exceeds threshold.
Embedding model preference: they want a compact, high-throughput embedding model (open-type) for cost reasons; willing to test Redwood-verified model + fallback to smaller quantized variant.
Vector DB: currently on Pinecone (standard tier). They asked about native connectors and pipeline examples for FAISS-based nightly jobs.
Throughput concerns: cold KV-cache on long context -> want guidance on prefix caching and batching to avoid token cost blowouts.
Integrations requested: sample ingestion pipeline (S3 -> batch embed -> upsert to Pinecone), example DAG (Airflow), and monitoring dashboard for token/latency costs.
Request for Drive: security FAQ, Hosted vs Dedicated pricing sheet, example POC SOW.
additional_context: Team: Head of Product (Evan Rhodes), Staff ML Engineer (Aisha Khan), Platform Lead (Marco Silva).
